Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
Lower abdominal (suprapubic) burning pain × 2 days, urinary frequency, pink-tinged urine, mild nausea, subjective fever/diaphoresis. No dysuria, no flank pain, bowels currently normal.  

Most likely acute uncomplicated cystitis; alternative considerations include early appendicitis and ectopic pregnancy (must be excluded despite Implanon).  

Plan: Empirical antibiotics (Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily × 3 days); home pregnancy test to confirm non-pregnant status; symptomatic care with paracetamol, hydration, cranberry juice. Safety-net advice: return or seek urgent care if pain worsens, fever develops, vomiting, or other concerning symptoms. Follow-up in a few days if no improvement.  

Management Plan
- Trimethoprim prescribed (1 tablet BID for 3 days)  
- Home pregnancy test advised today  
- Symptomatic relief: paracetamol, adequate fluids, cranberry juice  
- Safety-net instructions provided; review if no improvement/worsening within few days

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute cystitis – High likelihood: suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, hematuria, mild systemic features.  
2. Acute appendicitis – Moderate likelihood: infra-umbilical pain, worsening, mild nausea/fever; typical localization/RLQ signs absent.  
3. Ectopic pregnancy – Low–moderate likelihood: reproductive age, lower abdominal pain; Implanon ↓ risk but does not exclude; needs pregnancy test.
